subject: CardiaHealth: retention amendment & temporary log/export carveout
messages:
From: Helen Zhou <helen.zhou@cardiahealth.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: CardiaHealth retention request for backups + log TTL exception

Hi Priya / Karthik,

Thanks for taking this call yesterday. Per our internal compliance team: CardiaHealth needs a temporary retention carveout for a subset of customer backups and server logs tied to a regulatory review (HIPAA-adjacent evidence request). Specifically we need:

- A hold on scheduled backup purges for the customer namespace "cardia-prod" for 45 days (requested window: 2027-05-27 -> 2027-07-10).
- An exception to the standard log TTL for security/audit logs for the same namespace to preserve 90 days instead of the default 30 days.
- A list of subprocessors that will see the backed-up blobs for the duration of the hold and confirmation of any cross-border flows.

I've attached a short PDF that summarizes the scope (Cardia_Retention_Request.pdf) and the regulatory rationale. We need a mutual action plan with exact dates and owners so our legal team can sign off. Also please confirm whether Redwood can provide an export (S3 or encrypted archive) for escrow if full retention would cause policy issues.

Appreciate a short timeline and who on your side will be the point-of-contact for legal and ops.

Best,
Helen Zhou
Sr. IT Operations
CardiaHealth

--
Attachment: Cardia_Retention_Request.pdf (application/pdf, 112KB)

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Helen Zhou <helen.zhou@cardiahealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CardiaHealth retention request for backups + log TTL exception

Helen — thanks for the clear ask and the PDF. We're prepared to support a temporary carveout; below is a proposed plan so we can all agree on operational and legal steps: 

- Scope: hold applies only to the "cardia-prod" customer prefix; other customers unaffected.
- Purge hold window: 2027-05-27 00:00 UTC -> 2027-07-10 23:59 UTC (45 days).
- Logs: preserve security/audit logs for 90 days via an archived store. We'll keep standard hot logs at 30 days and write a daily archival job for the extra 60 days to an encrypted bucket.
- Subprocessors: attached CSV lists active subprocessors and the teams that will touch backups (DPA_Subprocessor_List.csv). Kimberly, can you confirm whether SafeStore will receive any backup blobs during the hold?
- Legal: we will accept an amendment to the DPA. I'll route a draft amendment to our legal and prod-ops; please send your signature contact and a DocuSign link if you have one.

Operational caveats: we will need a 12-hour blackout window to freeze purge jobs before the hold is applied so we don't have a race condition with scheduled deletion. We'll also require Cardia to approve an export schedule if you want an escrow copy (format choices: S3 encrypted tar.gz or Redacted JSON export).

Next steps (proposed):
1) Cardia sends procurement/DocuSign link (or signatories) and confirms acceptance of the dates.
2) Redwood provides amendment draft and subprocessor evidence within 48 hours.
3) Ops schedules purge hold (12-hour lead) and enables archival job.

I'll follow up with the legal draft and the subprocessor export.

Thanks — Priya
Priya Natarajan
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: DPA_Subprocessor_List.csv (text/csv, 4KB)

Subject: Re: CardiaHealth retention request for backups + log TTL exception

On Tue, May 25, 2027 at 10:03 AM Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> Operational caveats: we will need a 12-hour blackout window to freeze purge jobs before the hold is applied so we don't have a race condition with scheduled deletion.

Quick technical notes from infra: 
- Backup topology: cardia-prod backups are sharded across three retention classes (hot, warm, cold). The purge scheduler is TTL-based and runs hourly for hot/warm shards; cold shards are monthly.
- Implementation plan for a 45-day hold: mark the cardia-prod tag as "hold:retain-20270527-20270710" and skip it in the hourly purge loop. We'll run a one-time coordinator that verifies all shards have the tag before the window starts.
- Logs: for audit logs we can implement a daily export that appends to an encrypted long-term bucket (SSE-KMS). That export will be immutable for the 45-day window plus an additional 45 days to meet the 90-day retention requested (i.e., total preservation 90 days).
- Escrow export: S3 encrypted tar archive is simplest; size estimate for cardia-prod for 45 days: ~18GB compressed. We can provide checksums and a small index file.

Kimberly — note that SafeStore runs the offsite replication for cold-tier snapshots. If SafeStore will be in-scope for access during the hold, we need to flag a subprocessor audit and limit access to read-only via short-lived creds.

I'll prepare the backup-snapshot-plan doc and the purge-freeze runbook.

Thanks,
Karthik
Principal Systems Engineer, Infra
Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: backup-snapshot-plan.md (text/markdown, 6KB)

- We'll circulate a countersigned DocuSign if you can attach your amendment draft. Please include the exact start/end timestamps and the export format/options.
- We need evidence that SafeStore only has read-only access and that KMS keys are customer-managed or limited as described.

DocuSign link (for our internal tracking): https://docusign.net/AMENDMENT-Cardia-12345

Procurement expects a signed amendment within 72 hours so our compliance review can issue the internal hold.

Regards,
